thread:
maria: saw an OOM on a dedicated node running long-context CI workload (30k tokens). stack traces point at kv cache alloc hot path, not attention kernel.
kevin: which node / instance? can you paste the tail of the logs and any pmap/meminfo?
maria: node 4b2c, reproducer attached to the CI run. quick logs: 

```
2026-03-16T21:03:12Z runtime ERROR oom: failed alloc 18446744073709551615 bytes
2026-03-16T21:03:12Z runtime INFO kvcache: prefix_len=1452 entries=312345 mem_total=14.9GB mem_frag=27%
```

priya: ugh that unsigned wrap in the first line is ghastly (test harness). mem_total looks high. what was model and batch?
maria: model=redwood-medium-8k, batch=1, seq_len distribution skewed (one convo at 30k). KV cache footprint grew linearly with tokens as expected but we saw fragmentation spikes when entries were compacted.
sasha: can you capture heap profile and slab stats? try `curl http://node:6060/debug/pprof/heap` and `rd-slabctl dump`
maria: attaching pprof snippet: 

```
# top by inuse_space
100MiB  0.6%  kv_cache_node.go:412 allocateShard
82MiB   0.5%  kv_storage/arena.cc:128 alloc_chunk
48MiB   0.3%  kv_cache/compact.cc:91  compact_range
```

kevin: compact_range looks hot. are we doing partial compaction that leaves many tiny free spans -> fragmentation?
priya: yes, our current compaction only coalesces contiguous free slots but we keep per-prefix alignment which causes holes when long-prefixes are deleted.

maria: reco'd quick mitigation: 1) decrease max_prefetch for super-long prefixes 2) enable aggressive compaction threshold 3) a soft fallback when available_mem < reserve for kernels (deprioritize kv allocation).
sasha: can we implement a soft-degrade path where we still serve but stop populating KV for that request and mark response with `X-Redwood-KV-Skipped: true`? that avoids whole-node OOMs.
kevin: plus we should backoff retries and churn on eviction. propose adding `oom_action: fallback-no-kv` in routing policy for requests over N tokens.
priya: logging + observability checklist: emit a metric kv_reuse_skipped, kv_compact_count, kv_frag_ratio. add a high-cardinality tag for prefix_bucket (binned by length).
deploy-bot: created incident INC-2026-042: "kvcache memory growth -> OOM (node 4b2c)"
ops-bot: rolling alert: CPU/Memory above threshold on pool dedicated-gpu-3 (see dashboard)

maria: quick experiment patch I pushed to `eng-runtime/kv-soft-degrade` branch: 

```
# config snippet
kv_policy {
  max_prefetch_tokens: 4096
  compaction_threshold_bytes: 1048576  # 1MB
  frag_ratio_critical: 0.4
  oom_action: "fallback-no-kv"
  fallback_ttl_s: 30
}
```

kevin: nice. two safety concerns: 1) we must ensure kernel selection won't reallocate large KV block when fallback toggles off, 2) don't cause model mismatch (fallback should be transparent).
sasha: small perf note: switching to fallback-no-kv increases latency ~+40ms on median for long contexts but stable under OOM conditions.
priya: can we also add an emergency allocator reserve: `reserve_kv_heap_bytes=256MB` per process so the runtime never consumes host memory for large ephemeral allocs?
maria: added `reserve_kv_heap_bytes` to branch and a guard: if mem_avail < reserve -> set oom_action immediately.
kevin: please run the CI reproducer with that branch and collect the following: heap pprof, slab dump, and `perf top` sample during peak.
maria: running now, will paste results.

(3m later)
maria: CI run with branch completed without OOM. slab dump shows compaction_count doubled but frag_ratio remained < 0.28. heap footprint peaked at 10.1GB vs 14.9GB before.
kevin: great. can we ship as a canary to 10% of Dedicated pool with 15-min ramp and monitor kv_oom_rate, request_error_rate, and p50 latency?
sasha: also add an automatic rollback if kv_oom_rate > 0.1% or request_errors > 0.05% above baseline.
priya: i'll add the metrics and the alert runbook entries. ops, can you watch the canary?
ops-bot: scheduled canary rollout to pool `dedicated-gpu-3` at 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z, target 10% nodes, ramp 15m
